author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has directed Tesla to answer questions by Sept. 30 about how it certified the Cybercab as meeting federal vehicle-safety standards, Reuters reported Tuesday.

The agency is asking whether temporary human-driver controls or other equipment were used as part of Tesla’s compliance basis. The Cybercab was designed without conventional controls available to passengers, making the certification approach central to the inquiry.

NHTSA opened an Audit Query on Sept. 4 after Tesla deployed Cybercabs commercially in Austin. The agency said the review would examine the technical data and processes behind Tesla’s self-certification, including any conclusion that particular standards do not apply to automated vehicles.

The inquiry does not by itself establish a violation. NHTSA says existing federal safety standards remain in force while it works on rule changes involving equipment such as brake pedals, windshield wipers, lighting and rearview mirrors.
dek: The federal auto-safety agency is asking how Tesla concluded its driverless vehicle complied with existing standards, including whether temporary human controls factored into testing.
headline: NHTSA sets deadline for Tesla Cybercab certification answers
